nix store make-content-addressed gives the same path before and after these changes. But ca-derivations are not a thing yet, so yay, let's rebuild the world.

items.content_html:
This PR introduces an variety of changes to the smartd module:

  • Shellcheck validation of the notification script
  • Dynamic detection of the X11 session to send notifications to.
  • Systemd unit hardening
  • NixOS tests for all notification mechanisms + various device detection
  • Remove dbus package as an optional dep, replace with busctl from systemd

The changes should be backwards compatible with the exception of sendmail implementations that requires further relaxed hardening (if there are any).

Ref #377827

I've been working on a re-implementation of NixOS vars as part of the Google Summer of Code project, together with my mentor @Lassulus. For info about the API, check the README included with this PR.

Things done

This PR implements a basic CLI for working with vars, a NixOS module that can be used together with the CLI, and some simple examples. There's also a simple NixOS test.

A bunch of concepts in the API have temporary names. Feel free to suggest better ones!

We're about to introduce a third variant with the same copy-and-paste approach, so this is the right moment to unify.

This commit moves the nixos-rebuild-specialisations and nixos-rebuild-store-path tests into nixos/tests/nixos-rebuild/, extracting their identical machine definition and configuration.nix boilerplate into a common.nix module with a mkConfigFile helper.

I also moved nixos-rebuild-target-host there for co-location; since it's a two-node deploy test, it keeps its own scaffolding instead of importing common.nix, but it's all nice and tidy in the nixos/tests/nixos-rebuild/ directory.

Behavior of these tests does not change.

items.content_html:
First time creating a module. Creates a service and can also create files for tracing policies and configuration files. Based that off the apparmor module, since it felt like a really good way of doing it.

The service file is basically the one used by the Tetragon repo: https://github.com/cilium/tetragon/blob/main/install/linux-tarball/systemd/tetragon.service. It might need to be more secure before it gets merged. There might be some way of securing it to a non-root user as shown with version 1.6.0 for Kubernetes: https://tetragon.io/docs/installation/configuration/#run-the-operator-as-non-root

@gngram tetragon maintainer for visibility.

items.content_html:
Add a NixOS module for OpenList, a file list program supporting multiple storage providers, forked from Alist: https://github.com/OpenListTeam/OpenList

This PR adds services.openlist: a hardened systemd service with a freeform settings submodule, _secret support via genJqSecretsReplacementSnippet, TLS through systemd credentials, runtime config merging (mutableConfig), and extraPackages/extraFlags following RFC 42. It includes NixOS manual documentation, a NixOS test, and a release notes entry.
